pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: DeepSeek compatibility is broadened in two ways: OpenAI-compatible endpoints whose configured base URL contains "deepseek" now use the standard OpenAI SDK client even when the URL also looks Azure-hosted, and model IDs containing "deepseek-r1" are now classified like existing DeepSeek reasoner models in both provider handlers.

behavior_changes.description: When OpenAiHandler is configured with a base URL containing "deepseek" case-insensitively, it now constructs the standard OpenAI client. This check precedes the Azure-domain check, so a URL containing both "deepseek" and "azure.com" also takes the standard OpenAI client path rather than the AzureOpenAI path.
evidence: The new DeepSeek URL branch constructs OpenAI and is evaluated before the existing Azure branch.
The release note describes the intended outcome as enabling DeepSeek use in Azure.

citations.quoted_text: Fixed to be able to use DeepSeek in Azure.

behavior_changes.description: Models whose IDs contain "deepseek-r1" are now classified as DeepSeek reasoner models by both DeepSeekHandler and OpenAiHandler, causing them to enter the same subsequent reasoner-specific handling as IDs containing "deepseek-reasoner".
evidence: Both handlers extend the same reasoner-model predicate with the deepseek-r1 identifier.

important_symbols.reason: It controls which SDK client and API shape are selected from the configured base URL; branch precedence is central to the stated Azure DeepSeek compatibility change.
It expands reasoner-model recognition for OpenAI-compatible configurations to include deepseek-r1.
It applies the same deepseek-r1 reasoner classification in the dedicated DeepSeek provider, so consistency between the two handlers matters.
It records the intended user-facing purpose: making DeepSeek usable in Azure.

investigation_hints.description: Trace where OpenAiHandler is instantiated and how openAiBaseUrl is populated, especially for Azure-hosted DeepSeek deployments and URLs containing both identifying substrings.
Inspect all uses of isDeepseekReasoner after these predicates to determine the exact message conversion, streaming, and response behavior now applied to deepseek-r1 models.
Verify the OpenAI SDK's required client, authentication, URL, and API-version semantics for Azure-hosted DeepSeek endpoints; the code intentionally bypasses AzureOpenAI for matching URLs.

local_risks.description: Client selection relies on a broad substring and gives it precedence over the Azure-domain test. If an Azure-hosted DeepSeek endpoint actually requires the AzureOpenAI API shape, this branch would use the wrong client and could make requests fail or authenticate incorrectly; the required SDK semantics need verification.
